description: Found 2026-11-15 (bitstring split experiments). On fz-nml.11 31823421d: 'case <<1::72>> do <<x::72>> -> x end' panics in Rust at runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:716 'integer field too wide: 72' (exit 134 interp/run, 141 build). Elixir returns {:matched, 1}. field_end also refuses total > 64 on match (ir_runtime.rs:1503). Open question before building: fz integers are 64-bit, so the decision is whether a wide segment whose value fits (leading zero bits / sign extension) is accepted, and what a value that does not fit does -- Elixir has bignums, so exact parity may be impossible; the floor is that it is a loud fz error (compile-time when the size is constant, a raise at runtime), never a Rust panic. Needs a short proposal with the options before building.
title: An integer segment wider than 64 bits raises or works as in Elixir instead of panicking the runtime
